g.title: TTS_QSP
g.text: Takotsubo Syndrome — Quantitative Systems Pharmacology Map
apical ballooning as a THRESHOLD, not a location: one beta2-AR Gs→Gi switch evaluated at three receptor densities
inotrope benefit = drive added × fraction delivered without raising receptor phosphorylation · drug PK/PD · endpoints

g.title: cluster_trig
g.text: 1 · Trigger & susceptibility (the same surge does not produce the same disease in everybody)

g.title: cluster_cns
g.text: 2 · Brain-heart axis (limbic appraisal → brainstem → efferent sympathetic burst)

g.title: cluster_cat
g.text: 3 · Sympathoadrenal output & catecholamine kinetics (the agonist IDENTITY matters, not just the level)

g.title: cluster_field
g.text: 4 · Cardiac adrenoceptor FIELD — the apex-to-base density gradient is the ONLY inter-segment difference in this model

g.title: cluster_switch
g.text: 5 · THE THRESHOLD: beta2-AR stimulus trafficking (Gs → Gi). One function, three densities.

g.title: cluster_camp
g.text: 6 · cAMP-PKA compartment (per segment; the node every cAMP-route drug enters)

g.title: cluster_ca
g.text: 7 · Calcium handling & Ca2+ overload (the second, injury-producing consequence of the surge)

g.title: cluster_myo
g.text: 8 · Myofilament & segmental contractility (where levosimendan enters, bypassing cluster 6)

g.title: cluster_energy
g.text: 9 · Energetics, mitochondria, oxidative stress (why the deficit outlives the catecholamine)

g.title: cluster_micro
g.text: 10 · Coronary microvascular function (a REAL contributor, but not sufficient on its own)

g.title: cluster_inj
g.text: 11 · Sarcolemmal injury & troponin release (small rise, large dysfunction — the discordance is structural)

g.title: cluster_oed
g.text: 12 · Myocardial oedema & transient inflammation (the slow term that sets the WEEKS timescale)

g.title: cluster_mech
g.text: 13 · Regional mechanics → ballooning geometry (EMERGENT: no node here is prescribed a region)

g.title: cluster_lvot
g.text: 14 · Dynamic LVOT obstruction & mitral regurgitation (the term that flips the sign of beta-blockade)

g.title: cluster_nh
g.text: 16 · Neurohormonal response (the arm that ACE inhibition — not beta-blockade — enters)

g.title: cluster_ep
g.text: 17 · Electrophysiology: repolarisation, QT and torsade (the day-2-to-3 hazard window)

g.title: cluster_thr
g.text: 18 · Apical thrombus & embolism (stasis is a consequence of the geometry, so it is predictable)

g.title: cluster_rec
g.text: 19 · Recovery (a SIGNALLING lesion reverses; a necrotic one does not — hence weeks, not never)

g.title: cluster_drugA
g.text: 20 · Drugs A — cAMP-route inotropes/pressors: every one of these ADDS to the phosphorylation that made the disease

g.title: cluster_drugB
g.text: 21 · Drugs B — inotropy that bypasses the receptor (second factor of the product ≈ 1)

g.title: cluster_drugC
g.text: 22 · Drugs C — beta-blockade & alpha1 agonism: a CONDITIONAL sign, decided by the LVOT gradient term

g.title: cluster_drugD
g.text: 23 · Drugs D — RAAS blockade, decongestion, anticoagulation, adjuncts

g.title: cluster_mcs
g.text: 24 · Mechanical support (the choice is decided by the SAME gradient term, not by shock severity)

g.title: cluster_end
g.text: 25 · Clinical endpoints, InterTAK diagnostic score, outcome & recurrence

g.title: cluster_inf
g.text: 26 · Inference structure — four counterfactual integrators, so each mechanism's share is MEASURED not assumed

g.text: beta1 = beta2 >> alpha1 at low dose

g.text: ug/kg/min x 24 h; parent t1/2 ~1 h

g.text: for apical thrombus or high stasis
